clue.text: Advocacy group embracing criminal, regressive cause, for the most part

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold something within your arms, so one piece wraps around the other
regressive means going backwards, so this word is read from its end to its start
most but not all of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut and turned round
perp is American police slang for a perpetrator

explanation.surface: A lobbying outfit takes on a crook and a failing cause, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: Perp is American police slang for the perpetrator of a crime. A super PAC is a US political action committee allowed to raise unlimited funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A super PAC is a US political committee spending unlimited money to promote candidates or issues, which makes it a kind of lobbying organisation.

clue.text: Miltie, for one, is confused when abandoning Arkansas

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving something behind, so the state's letters are taken out

blocks.note: confused, as in not clear
AR is the postal abbreviation for Arkansas

explanation.surface: Someone named Miltie is muddled after leaving Arkansas.
explanation.walkthrough: UNCLEAR minus AR leaves UNCLE. Milton Berle, the early American TV comedian, was nicknamed Uncle Miltie.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedian Milton Berle's famous nickname was Uncle Miltie, so he is an example of someone called uncle.

clue.text: Nine bats eating inside of bug, producing boredom

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the letters before it are scrambled
something eating takes another thing inside it
the inside of a short word is its central letter alone

blocks.note: taken as written, then scrambled
the middle letter of this three-letter word

explanation.surface: Nine crazed creatures munch on an insect, and it is all rather tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like a noun for the creatures but works as the slang adjective for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French-derived word for listless weariness and dissatisfaction, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: One in disgrace for each vocal number soon adopted a pitch, rising

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one word goes inside another
in a down entry rising means read from bottom to top, so these letters run backwards

blocks.note: per means for each, as in a dollar per head
a number that is sung
anon is an old word for soon
taken as written
pitch is the black tarry substance

explanation.surface: A disgraced performer gets one song after another and is shortly given a sales pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: PER + SON(ANON)G, with ANON tucked into SONG, then A TAR read upwards as RATA.
explanation.definitionFit: Persona non grata is Latin for an unwelcome person, someone who has fallen out of favour.

clue.text: Payment, perhaps: only person under pressure gets an item of clothing

blocks.note: cash is one form of payment, hence perhaps
mere means only, as in a mere child
someone sweating, as people under pressure do

explanation.surface: A lone person paying up while stressed gets a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: The person under pressure is one who sweats, a 'sweater', which doubles as the garment itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A cashmere sweater is a knitted pullover made from fine goat wool, so it is a garment someone wears.

clue.text: Backing up, turned toward beverage

indicators.note: backing up means moving in reverse, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: to have turned toward something is to have faced it

explanation.surface: Someone reverses and turns to face a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaf, short for decaffeinated coffee, is a hot drink, so it is an example of a beverage.

clue.text: Quarterdeck has cold beer of inferior quality

blocks.note: split as deck (to knock DOWN) with a quarter, S for south, attached
C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: On a ship's quarterdeck, sailors drink cheap, poor beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads quarterdeck as the ship's raised rear deck; split into its two words, deck gives DOWN with the quarter S after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Downscale is American usage for cheap and low-end, aimed at less wealthy buyers, so it describes something lower in quality.

clue.text: Rated "for general audiences" in Alien: camera on fellow director

indicators.note: something alien is strange and foreign, so these letters are made strange by rearranging
in places the film rating inside the other letters

blocks.note: G is the US film rating for general audiences
taken as written, then scrambled

explanation.surface: A movie director's credits: Alien is rated G and filmed with a colleague behind the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites thinking of Ridley Scott's film; Alien is the anagram signal. CAMERA ON becomes COMANA-ER around the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-manager shares the job of running something with another person, so they are a joint director.

clue.text: Swell penalty

blocks.note: first meaning: excellent, in old-fashioned American slang
second meaning: money paid as punishment

explanation.walkthrough: Swell reads as a verb or a wave, but here it is the dated slang adjective for great.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both very good as an adjective and a monetary punishment as a noun.

clue.text: Capital's principal newsrooms nag corrupt politician

indicators.note: the principal letter of a word is its first, leading one
corrupt means spoiled or twisted, so these letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: the first letter of this word
taken as written, then scrambled

explanation.surface: In Washington, the press rooms harass a crooked legislator.
explanation.definitionFit: A congresswoman is a female member of the US Congress, an elected lawmaker and so a politician.

clue.text: Turmoil from the center, pal

blocks.note: a hub is the center of a wheel or of activity
bub is American slang for buddy or pal

explanation.surface: A friend feels the chaos coming from the middle of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A hubbub is a noisy confused commotion, a near synonym for turmoil and uproar.

clue.text: Deuterium offers protection for wombs

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the letters sit inside this word

blocks.note: the letters run inside this chemical name

explanation.surface: A heavy form of hydrogen is said to shield wombs, like some pseudo-medical claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Uteri is the Latin plural of uterus, the medical name for the womb.

clue.text: Except for the speed of light, universe with pull (gravity) is getting through

indicators.note: except for means leaving that thing out, so the physics symbol is removed

blocks.note: the cosmos is the universe
c is the physics symbol for the speed of light
having an in means having pull or influence
g is the symbol for gravitational acceleration

explanation.surface: A physics claim: with gravity tugging, the universe lets things pass, apart from light speed.
explanation.walkthrough: COSMOS loses its C, then IN and G are added.
explanation.definitionFit: To osmose is to pass through a membrane by osmosis, so osmosing means seeping or passing through.

clue.text: Fatal geometric configuration of grass, shorts and onions?

definitions.text: Fatal geometric configuration of grass, shorts and onions?

blocks.note: surface reading: a deadly three-cornered shape
setter's reading: each item takes the name of the same Atlantic island group, so the deadly shape belongs to those islands

explanation.walkthrough: Grass, shorts and onions are all called Bermuda, and the notorious stretch of sea where ships vanish is named after that island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bermuda Triangle is a region of the Atlantic legendary for ships and planes disappearing, hence fatal and three-cornered.

clue.text: Ugly crone (peculiar, heartless) is overcome again

indicators.note: ugly suggests something misshapen, so these letters are deformed into a new order
without a heart, the central letter of the word is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
queer in its old sense of odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: A hideous, odd, cruel old hag is defeated once more.
explanation.walkthrough: QUEER loses its middle E to give QUER, which is scrambled with CRONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconquer is to conquer a second time, and conquering is defeating, so it means to defeat again.

clue.text: Vishnu's foot — where the E might be dug up?

indicators.note: in a down entry the foot of a word is its bottom, final letter

blocks.note: the last letter of the god's name
in the alphabet E comes right next to D

explanation.surface: A question about where the Hindu god's footprint, or some letter E, could be excavated.
explanation.walkthrough: E follows D in the alphabet, so it is NEAR THE D.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something is to dig it out of the ground, so unearthed means excavated.

clue.text: While this may be true, it is assumed by Steven Soderbergh

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on, so the phrase sits inside the name

blocks.note: the letters run across the director's first and last names

explanation.surface: A film director takes some claim for granted, though it may be true.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so is a concessive phrase meaning nevertheless, granting a point while still disagreeing.

clue.text: German composer with horrible greed, or else evidence of a college education

indicators.note: horrible means ghastly and distorted, so these letters are pulled into a different order

blocks.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the German Baroque composer
taken as written, then scrambled

explanation.surface: A greedy German composer issues a threat: or else.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor's degree is the undergraduate qualification awarded on completing college, so it proves that schooling.

clue.text: Hatch plots to mix gin and 11

indicators.note: to mix things is to stir them together, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the answer to 11 Across

explanation.surface: A schemer stirs gin with something to cook up a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 11 stands for that entry's answer, which joins GIN as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrigue is to scheme secretly, which is to hatch plots against someone.

clue.text: In the beginning, cook requires barrels

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
to ask for something is to require it

explanation.surface: A chef first of all needs barrels for the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Casks are wooden barrels for holding liquids such as wine or beer, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Xerxes' grandfather contributed to fancy ruse

indicators.note: something contributed to two words is part of both, so the name spans them

blocks.note: the letters run across these two words

explanation.surface: A Persian king's grandfather helped devise an elaborate trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyrus the Great founded the Persian empire; his daughter Atossa was mother of Xerxes I, making Cyrus his grandfather.

clue.text: Yankee in list ruined pens

indicators.note: in places the military letter inside the other letters
something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written, then scrambled

explanation.surface: An American on a spoiled roster writes things down.
explanation.definitionFit: Styli are pointed writing instruments, the plural of stylus, used for marking wax or screens like a pen.

clue.text: Zany solo in Scandinavian city

indicators.note: zany means wildly silly, so these letters are thrown into a crazy order

blocks.note: taken as written, then scrambled

explanation.surface: A comic one-person act performed in a Nordic town.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway, so it is an example of a city in Scandinavia.

clue.text: Just like some winds in spirit, the flower touches you at first

indicators.note: in places the phrase about the flower inside the word for spirit
at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the soul is a person's spirit
taken as written
an aster is a daisy-like flower
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A spirit and a flower brushing against you, as gently as a breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' sits on the definition so that the clue keeps its alphabetical starting letter J; the clues open with A to Z in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Winds blowing from the southeast are called southeasterly, so the word describes a type of wind's direction.

clue.text: Kept a rowboat going, or flew starting late

indicators.note: a word that starts late has lost its opening letter

blocks.note: to soar is to fly high

explanation.surface: Someone either rowed a boat or took off late in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: SOARED without its first letter gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To oar is to propel a boat with oars, so oared means rowed it along.

clue.text: Like nearly half of these clues, almost, unconscious habit reveals what can be found in these clues

definitions.text: what can be found in these clues

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the final letter is removed

blocks.clueFragment: Like nearly half of these clues
blocks.note: twelve of the twenty-six clues run horizontally in the grid
a tic is an involuntary twitch or habit

explanation.surface: A self-referring puzzle comment hinting at a hidden pattern in the clues.
explanation.walkthrough: ACROSS loses its last S, then TIC is added. The clues' first letters run A to Z in order, a pattern hidden in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a text whose initial letters spell something; here the clue openings spell the alphabet.
